anomalies.description: A sudden violent structural failure or explosion occurs: the large tanker truck rapidly collapses/ruptures from left to right across frames 6–12, with visible deformation, detachment of parts, and rapid outward movement of debris and smoke/dust—consistent with an instantaneous blast event. The person in red cap remains stationary but appears to react (slight flinch/posture shift) as the event unfolds, indicating sudden onset. No prior warning or gradual motion is observed; the change is abrupt and catastrophic.

A person in white uniform and red cap approaches a fuel hose near a vehicle, then suddenly crouches and appears to be struck or thrown backward violently (frames 8–10), suggesting an explosion or sudden release of pressure—consistent with a fuel-related blast. No visible fire or smoke in these frames, but the abrupt, unexplained violent motion and posture (falling backward without contact) strongly indicate an incident such as a fuel vapor explosion or hose rupture.

A sudden bright flash and rapid ejection of debris occur at ~55.0s, consistent with an explosion: a person near the vehicle is violently thrown backward, followed by visible smoke/dust cloud and scattered fragments. The event is instantaneous and matches the expected explosion signature (bright flash, outward-flying debris, immediate large smoke/dust cloud).

post_cbt.description: Sudden bright flash and violent disruption at frame 8 (timestamp ~84s), followed by rapid camera shake, blurring, and debris/dust cloud in frames 9–11 — consistent with an instantaneous explosion: intense light, outward-flying fragments, and immediate loss of scene clarity.

original_descriptions.description: Sudden bright flash and violent disruption at frame 8 (timestamp ~84s), followed by rapid camera shake, blurring, and debris/dust cloud in frames 9–11 — consistent with an instantaneous explosion: intense light, outward-flying fragments, and immediate loss of scene clarity.

Sudden bright flash followed by rapid outward ejection of debris and formation of a dense smoke/dust cloud—consistent with an explosion occurring at ~86s–87s. Debris is visibly scattered across the floor, and the intensity and instantaneous onset match the expected anomaly type.

anomalies.description: A sudden violent structural failure or explosion occurs: the large tanker truck rapidly collapses/ruptures from left to right across frames 6–12, with visible deformation, detachment of parts, and rapid outward movement of debris and smoke/dust—consistent with an instantaneous blast event. Sudden bright flash followed by rapid outward ejection of debris and formation of a dense smoke/dust cloud—consistent with an explosion occurring at ~86s–87s. Debris is visibly scattered across the floor, and the intensity and instantaneous onset match the expected anomaly type.

post_bue.description: A sudden violent structural failure or explosion occurs: the large tanker truck rapidly collapses/ruptures from left to right across frames 6–12, with visible deformation, detachment of parts, and rapid outward movement of debris and smoke/dust—consistent with an instantaneous blast event. The person in red cap remains stationary but appears to react (slight flinch/posture shift) as the event unfolds, indicating sudden onset. No prior warning or gradual motion is observed; the change is abrupt and catastrophic.

post_bue.description: A sudden bright flash and rapid expansion of light/energy emanates from the front of the yellow vehicle between frames 4 and 5 (around 47–48s), followed by visible debris scattering outward and a rapidly growing smoke/dust cloud—consistent with an explosion. The vehicle's front end appears severely damaged/disrupted immediately after the flash, and no prior ignition source or collision is observed.

A person in white uniform and red cap approaches a fuel hose near a vehicle, then suddenly crouches and appears to be struck or thrown backward violently (frames 8–10), suggesting an explosion or sudden release of pressure—consistent with a fuel-related blast. No visible fire or smoke in these frames, but the abrupt, unexplained violent motion and posture (falling backward without contact) strongly indicate an incident such as a fuel vapor explosion or hose rupture.

A sudden bright flash and rapid ejection of debris occur at ~55.0s, consistent with an explosion: a person near the vehicle is violently thrown backward, followed by visible smoke/dust cloud and scattered fragments. The event is instantaneous and matches the expected explosion signature (bright flash, outward-flying debris, immediate large smoke/dust cloud).
